messages:
Ravi Kaur: Kestrel Ops reached out — they want a focused migration POC from PromptlyAI. Main asks: output parity for structured JSON outputs, per-route billing granularity, and EU data residency. Can we list immediate blockers?
Nina Lopez: quick list: (1) prove stop-token and streaming parity, (2) shared seed/sample determinism, (3) Dedicated capacity + EU residency, (4) customer-supplied KMS and audit log retention.
Jared Kim: For determinism: PromptlyAI supports seeded sampling on their v1 endpoints. We should offer a seeded run mode in the harness and show repeatability. propose harness: 40 prompts x 5 seeds each.
Priya Singh: Security side: they want KMS import, HSM-backed key option, and proof of data-at-rest AES-256. Also DPA + SOC2 report. Legal asked if we can redact customer PII during logs for the POC.
Ravi Kaur: They also requested billing by sub-route (generate vs embed) and the ability to tag usage to a client project id. Is that doable on Dedicated?
Nina Lopez: Yes. Dedicated supports per-route metering + project tags. We'll need to add a short invoice example showing line items and how credits apply during the migration window.
Jared Kim: Perf concerns: they said PromptlyAI guaranteed 100 rps, they need sustained 35 rps with bursts to 120. We'll run a smoke test in eu-west-1 Dedicated cluster and publish p50/p95.
Priya Singh: Security mitigation for the POC: ephemeral keys, no raw request body stored, and restricted access to logs. Also provide an incident contact (sec-ops@redwood.example).
Ravi Kaur: Customer wants an auto-fallback if our new model exhibits regressions — webhook + automatic switch to a fallback model is required for production parity. Can we commit for the POC?
Nina Lopez: Yes we can configure rollout with automatic fallback for the POC scope. I'll document the policy and webhook payloads.
infra-bot: cluster-create: ephemeral-dedicated-eu-west-1 created. creds rotated; will push secret path to vault.
Jared Kim: I'll own the harness: plan = ingest their top-60 prompts (they'll share), run PromptlyAI baseline + r-large + r-quant, diff tokens, stop-token tests, seeded runs, and streaming vs non-streaming comparisons. Acceptance: >= 93% intent match and no more than 3% higher hallucination rate.
Priya Singh: Add an edge-case test for nested terminators (e.g. "<END>", "</end>") — those caused mismatches before.
Ravi Kaur: Timeline suggestion: Day 0-1: NDA/DPA sign + infra creds. Day 2-4: prompt ingest + seeded runs. Day 5-6: analysis + parity decision.
Nina Lopez: Pricing ask: they want 3-month committed Dedicated with a migration rebate if parity achieved within 30 days. I'll draft a term sheet for finance review.
Jared Kim: Example curl for smoke test (will put real values in secure vault):
```
curl -s -X POST https://eu.api.redwood/v1/generate
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY"
  -H "Content-Type: application/json"
  -d '{"model":"r-large","input":"${PROMPT}","stop":["<END>"],"seed":12345,"stream":false}'
```
Priya Singh: We'll attach SOC2 + pen-test summary after legal clears the DPA. For POC only we can accept a limited-scope DPA and redact log retention details.
Ravi Kaur: Owners: Jared (harness + perf), Priya (security + DPA), Nina (pricing + contract), Ravi (customer comms). I'll send a recap email and schedule a kickoff.
Nina Lopez: One more note 5 - they asked about tokenization differences for curly braces and emojis. Include a token-diff step and a mapping doc.
Jared Kim: added. I'll export token diffs and examples.
Ravi Kaur: Thanks team. Will wait for legal on DPA then we can start.
